entire_inventory_record.source_text:
Barrier functions verify a closed loop; control barrier functions let us design one, exactly as Sontag's control Lyapunov functions extend Lyapunov functions. Take the control-affine system $\dot x=f(x)+g(x)u$ with $f,g$ locally Lipschitz, $x\in D\subset\mathbb R^n$, $u\in U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$. Along any trajectory
    $$\dot h(x,u)=L_fh(x)+L_gh(x)\,u,$$
    which is affine in $u$. This single fact is why CBF conditions become linear constraints and safety filters become quadratic programs.

hypotheses: h is the continuously differentiable barrier of the immediately following definition; the trajectory is an existing differentiable solution (or the selected absolutely continuous/a.e. solution under its explicit domain assumptions).

The velocity is f(x)+g(x)u; g(x) is a continuous linear map in the input; finite real coordinate specialization gives the printed row Lie derivative. Local Lipschitz f,g are source assumptions and are not needed for the pointwise algebra.
